standard_prerequisites.name: Polychromatic colourings and the parameter m_H(k)
standard_prerequisites.statement: A polychromatic k-colouring of a hypergraph puts a vertex of every one of the k colour classes into every hyperedge; m_H(k) is the least m such that every member of the family has a polychromatic k-colouring after all edges of size below m are deleted, and it is infinity when no such m exists.
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the counted quantity m_{A*}(k) and the meaning of an edge that is not polychromatic in the dual family.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: source lines 120 and 123-129, retained as context

standard_prerequisites.name: Finite plane point sets, strips and slight perturbation
standard_prerequisites.statement: A finite vertex set in the plane and finitely many axis-parallel strips realise the dual family A-star, whose vertices are the strips and whose edges are the sets of strips containing one point. Finitely many parallel strips can be perturbed a little so that no two of them coincide, while every nonempty region of their common intersection still captures the same families.
standard_prerequisites.use: The perturbation sentence at source line 479 keeps the four families of copies distinct as vertices of A-star and keeps the private part of each pair intersection captured by exactly the two corresponding families.
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: parenthetical sentence in the counted proof, source line 479

standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary finite counting and the pigeonhole principle
standard_prerequisites.statement: A set of c vertices carries at most c colours, so at least k minus c of the k colours are absent from it; four subsets of a k-element set whose sizes sum to more than k cannot be pairwise disjoint.
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the more-than-k/4 missing colours per family and the shared missing colour of two families in the counted proof.

core_obligations: Realise the four axis-parallel strips so that each of the six pairs has a part of its intersection that is disjoint from the other two original strips, and read each pair of copy-families as one point-determined edge of the dual family A-star of size 2(ceil(3k/4)-1).
Count the colours absent from one family of copies: ceil(3k/4)-1 vertices carry at most that many colours, so strictly more than k/4 of the k colours are missing from that family.

Pigeonhole the four missing-colour sets to obtain one colour absent from two families at once, so the corresponding edge of size 2(ceil(3k/4)-1) is not polychromatic, and conclude 2(ceil(3k/4)-1)+1 <= m_{A*}(k).

proof_roadmap.step: Fix ceil(3k/4)-1 copies of each of the four strips {0<x<2}, {1<x<3}, {0<y<2}, {1<y<3}; every pair of these has a private part of its intersection, and small perturbations make the copies distinct as vertices.
Take the dual hypergraph on these 4(ceil(3k/4)-1) strips with all point-determined edges; each family leaves more than k/4 colours unused, so two families leave the same colour unused.
The point in the private part of that pair of strips yields an edge of size 2(ceil(3k/4)-1) missing one colour, hence not polychromatic, and the strict lower bound follows.

difficulty_reason: The counted object is the dual family A-star of axis-parallel strips (source lines 203-204): its vertices are the strips and its edges are the point-determined sets of strips that contain a point, so the obstruction is built in the primal plane and then read in the dual. The crux is the arrangement fixed at source line 479, where four strips are chosen so that each of their six pairs has a part of its intersection disjoint from the other two strips, which turns each pair of copy-families into a single edge of A-star of size 2(ceil(3k/4)-1). The closing step at source line 481 is not the usual one-family pigeonhole: a family has only ceil(3k/4)-1 vertices, hence at most that many colours and strictly more than k/4 missing colours, and only the sum over four such missing-colour sets forces two families to share an absent colour. Merely counting vertices of the arrangement, or quoting a Ramsey-type homogeneity statement, does not produce the factor 2(ceil(3k/4)-1)+1.

compared.difference: The only public item of this article counts the three-part infinite arithmetic-progression theorem: extendable difference sets are embedded into octant hypergraphs and one part is proved infinite. It is about difference sets and octants in R^3, not about strips, shallow hitting sets or the parameter m_{A*}(k), and no step of it is used here.

The prepared strip target is a non-existence theorem for 2-shallow hitting sets in the m-uniform members of the primal strip family A, proved by an eleven-cluster gadget with two figures. This target is a strict lower bound for the polychromatic parameter of the dual family A-star and is proved by a four-family pigeonhole on missing colours; neither statement implies the other.

The bottomless-rectangle target refutes 3-shallow hitting sets for a different range family B by an A/B/C gadget with a two-case split; it shares neither the family, the parameter nor the construction with this item.

editorial_scope: One counted lower bound for the dual axis-parallel strip family: 2(ceil(3k/4)-1)+1 <= m_{A*}(k), with the article's complete four-family counting proof. The primal strip and bottomless non-existence theorems, the A-plus and A_s bounds, both arithmetic-progression theorems and the printed corollary after s_strip are not counted.
